$comment: SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH for the training/compile parameter contract. Read directly by the browser, the start-training edge function, and the Python pipeline — no codegen. See .scratch/train-param-contract/issues/05. A conformance test asserts every train key exists in ultralytics DEFAULT_CFG_DICT for the pinned version.

capability.title: Cannot reach a working HEF — YOLO26 pipeline not built
capability.text: YOLO26 removes Distribution Focal Loss and defaults to an NMS-free one-to-one head, so its box branch is 4 channels — the on-chip meta_arch=yolov8 decoder needs a 64-channel DFL box. Training, export and compile all report success and the device then counts zero.
capability.status: YOLO26 → Hailo-8L produces an undeployable HEF

capability.title: Compiles with the extra branch silently removed
capability.text: The head detector classifies this as detection, so it is given on-chip NMS and the keypoint/angle branch is dropped without an error. Verified against yolo11n-pose.
capability.status: loses its extra branch in compile

capability.title: BSCP pipeline supported
capability.text: YOLO11 detection has a validated Hailo-8L path: 64-channel DFL box, on-chip NMS via meta_arch=yolov8.
capability.status: BSCP Hailo pipeline available for selected model

capability.title: Host-side decode required
capability.text: Compiles on the raw path; mask decode stays on the host, which costs frame rate on the device.

capability.title: Task pipeline not validated
capability.text: Training is available, but this task has no validated BSCP path to a Hailo-8L artifact.
capability.status: BSCP deployment path not yet validated

params.label: Epochs
params.help: How many passes over the dataset. The primary lever on both cost and fit — too few underfits, too many overfits and burns Colab time.

params.label: Image size
params.help: Training resolution, a multiple of 32. The compile run inherits this value as its input shape — they can never disagree.

params.label: Batch size
params.help: Images per step. 'auto' lets ultralytics size it to the GPU it actually gets, which varies between Colab sessions.

params.label: Optimizer
params.help: The algorithm that updates the weights. Pinned to AdamW because 'auto' switches to an experimental optimizer once a run passes ~10,000 iterations and silently discards your learning rate — one release of it crashed at epoch 1.

params.label: Learning rate
params.help: Initial learning rate. ~0.001 suits AdamW fine-tuning from a pretrained checkpoint; larger values destabilise a small dataset.

params.label: Patience
params.help: Stop after this many epochs without improvement. On a small dataset this is usually what actually ends the run, not the epoch count.

params.label: Seed
params.help: Fixes the random draw so two runs can be compared. Required by the experiment discipline for any result you intend to cite.

params.label: Deterministic
params.help: A seed alone does not make a run reproducible — this is what does. Turn it off only if you need the speed and do not intend to compare the result.

params.label: Checkpoint every
params.help: Save a checkpoint every N epochs. Colab sessions die mid-run — this repo has lost one at epoch 196 — and a checkpoint turns that into a resume instead of a restart.

params.label: Close mosaic
params.help: Disable mosaic augmentation for the final N epochs, so validation metrics reflect deployment-shaped images rather than collages.

params.label: Dataset fraction
params.help: Train on a subset. Useful for a deliberate smoke test — and the quietest footgun here, because a value left over from one produces a plausible but under-trained model.

params.label: Freeze layers
params.help: Freeze the first N backbone layers. The natural lever when the dataset is small and the pretrained features are already close.

params.label: Classes
params.help: Read from the dataset manifest. Not editable — the class list must match the compile config and the edge decoder exactly, and a mismatch is a hard runtime error on the device.

params.label: single_cls
params.help: Collapses every class into one. The whole downstream contract is two classes — the labelmap, the on-chip NMS config and the edge runtime — so a run with this set would train, export, compile, deploy, and be wrong.

params.label: Calibration set
params.help: The compile calibrates on the images the run already holds — its dataset's val split, train as fallback. No curated onsite set is registered anywhere a Colab session can fetch by name, so choosing one here would name images the compile could not load. Register the onsite frames as a dataset first, then this becomes a field again.

params.label: Calibration images
params.help: How many calibration images to use. Optimization level 2 expects at least 1024 — fewer, and its fine-tuning step has too little to work with.

params.label: Optimization level
params.help: 0 is basic quantization, proven here. 2 is quantization-aware FINE-TUNING — four epochs over 1024 images — which wants a GPU; without one the compiler silently drops back to 0, and a diverging fine-tune is the known cause of a dead HEF.

params.label: NMS score threshold
params.help: A hard floor baked into the HEF: nothing scoring below this can ever leave the model, so it caps what the flagging band can see. Kept low deliberately.

params.label: NMS IoU threshold
params.help: How much two boxes may overlap before one is suppressed. Kept high so two sacks touching each other are not merged into one detection.

params.label: Max detections per class
params.help: Sizes the output buffer, so it truncates rather than warns: a frame busier than this silently loses its tail.

params.label: Input conversion
params.help: Nothing applies it. The compile's model script sets normalization only (scripts/compile_clientrunner.py:225-228), so a conversion chosen here would be dropped in silence — and a silent RGB/BGR mismatch degrades every score without ever raising an error. It needs an input_conversion() line in that model script before it can be offered.

params.label: Compile seed
params.help: The DFC ClientRunner recipe takes no seed (scripts/compile_clientrunner.py), so a value here would fix nothing while implying a reproducibility the compile cannot give.

params.label: Run FP32-vs-INT8 check
params.help: Nothing in the run measures it. The compile parses, quantizes and compiles (scripts/compile_clientrunner.py); no step compares the model before and after quantization, so this switch would promise a check that never runs.

params.label: Compiler wheel
params.help: The gated DFC wheel the run installs, named from the pinned toolchain version rather than typed per run — so the compiler build and the recipe proven against it can never disagree. Typed per run, it was simply never sent, and every compile failed on its absence.

params.label: Input shape
params.help: Taken from the run that produced the ONNX. A compile cannot use a different input size than the model was trained at.

params.label: Regression length
params.help: The DFL bin count, fixed by the architecture at box_channels/4. Not a preference — a wrong value produces correctly-scored boxes in the wrong places.

params.label: Compiler profile
params.help: The named, versioned compile recipe implied by the chosen model and task.

params.label: Compression level
params.help: Pinned to 0. Four-bit weight compression trades accuracy for frame rate, which this line does not need.
